evals.prompt: Create a 3-year financial model for a SaaS startup. Year 1: $500K revenue, 40% growth rate. Include revenue, COGS (30% of revenue), gross profit, OpEx ($200K flat), EBITDA, and a revenue growth chart. Save to /tmp/saas_model.xlsx
evals.expected_output: An Excel file is created via build_xlsx.new_workbook(theme='ib') with a properly structured financial model using Excel formulas (not hardcoded values), ib-theme typography, and zero formula errors.
expectations: Uses build_xlsx.new_workbook(theme='ib') as the entry point (not raw openpyxl.Workbook)
Revenue projections use Excel growth formulas like =B5*(1+$B$6) referencing assumption cells
All cells are written via write_table / write_section_header / write_title_banner (no raw Font/PatternFill)
save_and_validate() is called instead of wb.save() and the returned report has status=='pass' and slop_score<=10
The resulting file has Arial 10 body, hidden gridlines, and a non-default sheet tab name

evals.prompt: I have a sales data file at /data/sales_2025.xlsx with columns: Date, Region, Product, Units, UnitPrice. Analyze it: give me total revenue by region, top 5 products by units sold, and monthly revenue trend. Show the results.
evals.expected_output: pandas is used to load and analyze the Excel data, producing aggregated statistics by region, a top-5 product ranking, and a monthly trend summary displayed clearly to the user.
expectations: Uses pandas pd.read_excel() to load the file
Computes total revenue (Units * UnitPrice) grouped by Region
Identifies top 5 products by total Units sold
Computes monthly revenue trend by resampling or grouping by month
Presents results in a readable format (table or summary)

evals.prompt: Add a new sheet called 'Assumptions' to /tmp/existing_model.xlsx with the following parameters: Revenue Growth Rate = 15%, Discount Rate = 10%, Tax Rate = 25%. Use the theme's input styling for cells that need user attention. Don't break the existing sheets.
evals.expected_output: openpyxl loads the existing workbook, build_xlsx.apply_theme+new_sheet adds a new 'Assumptions' sheet whose value cells use the theme input style, and the save_and_validate() pipeline passes without modifying existing sheets.
expectations: Uses openpyxl load_workbook() to open the existing file without data_only=True
Calls theme.apply_theme(wb, 'ib') before touching content so named styles are available
Creates a new sheet named 'Assumptions' via build_xlsx.new_sheet
Assumption value cells use style_name('ib','input') (blue Macabacus text, right-aligned, numeric format)
save_and_validate() returns status=='pass'
Existing sheets in the workbook are preserved unchanged

evals.prompt: Build a SaaS product metrics dashboard at /tmp/saas_dash.xlsx using theme='saas'. Include a KPI band with 4 cards (MRR, Active Users, Churn, NPS) and a weekly trend table. Verify it passes validate_xlsx.py.
evals.expected_output: build_xlsx.new_workbook(theme='saas') is used, write_kpi_band draws the 4 cards, write_table draws the weekly trend, and save_and_validate returns status='pass' with slop_score<=10.
expectations: new_workbook(theme='saas') is called (not ib)
The file uses the saas palette (indigo #6366F1 accent, slate ink #0F172A, emerald #10B981)
KPI band is created via write_kpi_band with 4 tuples
Weekly trend uses write_table with a formula column (net = new - churn)
save_and_validate returns status='pass'
validate_xlsx.py reports theme-appropriate body font (Aptos) on content cells

evals.prompt: Build a 3-statement financial model from templates/financial-model-skeleton.xlsx. Populate Assumptions with starting ARR $15mm, growth rates 45/35/30/25%, margins 72/74/75/76/77%, OpEx ratio 65/58/52/48/45%. Save to /tmp/3stmt.xlsx and ensure no forbidden terms and zero style violations.
evals.expected_output: build_xlsx.load_template('financial-model-skeleton', theme='ib') loads the skeleton, Assumptions cells are filled with numeric values (not strings), save_and_validate passes with zero formula errors and zero forbidden-term hits.
expectations: load_template('financial-model-skeleton', theme='ib') is used
Only pre-existing Assumptions cells are written (no new ad-hoc sheets)
No forbidden terms like 'TBD', 'revolutionary', or 'cutting-edge' appear in any cell
save_and_validate() returns status='pass', slop_score<=10, and recalc.status=='success'
The saved file still has the skeleton's tab colors, freeze panes, and title banner intact

evals.prompt: Create an engineering parameter sheet at /tmp/e101.xlsx using theme='engineering' for heat exchanger E-101. Include Design pressure 35 bar(g), Design temperature 150°C, Flow rate 12000 kg/h, with a Spec/Actual/Delta pattern and SI unit column. Validate the output.
evals.expected_output: new_workbook(theme='engineering') is used, write_section_header + write_table produce a parameter table with a Unit column, and save_and_validate returns status='pass'.
expectations: new_workbook(theme='engineering') is the entry point
The body font on content cells is Consolas (engineering theme)
Headers follow the Calibri 11 bold pattern from the engineering theme
A 'Unit' column is present between the label and the Spec column
Delta column contains an Excel formula like =E{i}-D{i}
save_and_validate() returns status='pass' with slop_score<=10
